row.scim_price_text: Premium: from $6/active user/mo + 3%/booking (Travel and Spend); $99/mo platform fee + 3%/booking (Travel only)
row.evidence: Perk's developer docs say "SCIM user provisioning is a Premium or Pro feature", and the pricing page lists Premium (from $6 per active user/month) as the first paid tier, with SSO included.
row.notes: TravelPerk rebranded to Perk; travelperk.com redirects to perk.com and the Okta/Entra gallery apps are still named TravelPerk. Starter ($0 platform fee, 5% per booking) is a travel-only free tier, so Premium is the team plan and SCIM has no upcharge over it. Pricing is per active user (anyone submitting or reviewing expenses in a month) plus booking fees, shown as 'Starting at'; billing period not stated. Travel-only plans use a flat platform fee (Premium $99/mo, Pro $299/mo). SCIM API is called with an admin API key; only one provisioning system (SCIM or an HR integration such as BambooHR) can run at a time; roles cannot be provisioned (everyone lands as traveler) and groups are not supported. Docs only document Okta and Azure/Entra apps; the generic SCIM API works for any client. Open API (REST) is Pro-only on the pricing page.

plans.name: Starter (Travel only)
plans.notes: Only on the Travel tab. SSO absent from Starter feature list; SCIM is Premium or Pro.

plans.name: Premium
plans.price_text: Starting at $6/month per active user + 3%/booking (Travel and Spend); Travel only: $99/month platform fee + 3%/booking
plans.notes: Spend-only Premium is listed from $11/active user/month (Spend tab). user_api false refers to the Open API, which the pricing page excludes from Premium.

plans.name: Pro
plans.price_text: Starting at $8/month per active user + 3%/booking (Travel and Spend); Travel only: $299/month platform fee + 3%/booking

auth.token_source: Admin API key (Settings > Developer > Travel tools), sent as 'Authorization: apikey <key>'; Okta/Entra apps use an OAuth authorize flow signed in as an account admin or developer

deprovision.data_retained: Inactive user disappears from the platform until reactivated; users with pending trips cannot be deactivated.

custom.how: travelperk extension (gender, dateOfBirth, travelPolicy, invoiceProfiles, emergencyContact, approvers, countryOfResidence, travelDocuments, company, lineManagerEmail, uniqueId, costCenterCode); expense extension (policyId, creditor, legalEntityId, approvalThreshold, ignoreManagerInRequests); perkcustomfields extension for account-specific custom fields

attributes.notes: Full list from the developer User object model page; Entra tutorial lists the default mapped subset.

roles.how: All users are provisioned as travelers; role changes are manual or via CSV.

rate_limits.text: Throttled; docs advise exponential backoff on 429 responses. No numeric limit stated in the pages read.

limitations.text: Only one user provisioning system can run at a time: an HR integration such as BambooHR must be removed before SCIM runs.
Groups are not supported; the groups attribute is always empty.
Users with pending trips cannot be deactivated.

webhooks_user_events.notes: Webhook events listed are invoice.issued and trip.created/updated only.

user_api.notes: User management is done through the SCIM API (documented above). A changelog announces a read-only Users API for trip travellers, and the pricing page puts the 'Open API' on Pro only, but no current non-SCIM user endpoint reference was found.

okta.notes: OIN page marks SAML, SWA, SCIM, Create, Update and Deactivate as checked (read from page markup); Group Push not checked.

fallbacks.other_sync: HR integrations (e.g. BambooHR) can provision users instead of SCIM; only one provisioning system at a time

conflicts.text: The 2019-era SCIM launch changelog lists 'Delete Users', but the current SCIM reference documents create, get, list, PUT and PATCH only, with deactivation via active=false; delete is recorded as null.

The getting-started guide lists 'A Perk account with Premium plan' as the prerequisite while the SCIM overview and the Entra tutorial say Premium or Pro; consistent with Premium being the lowest SCIM tier.

open_questions: Docs do not say whether deactivation frees a paid seat (pricing is per active user, i.e. anyone submitting or reviewing expenses in a month).
Whether SCIM DELETE is still supported (old changelog) is not in the current reference.
Google Workspace, OneLogin and JumpCloud catalogue apps not checked (support.perk.com and jumpcloud.com block plain requests).
No numeric SCIM rate limit or token expiry documented.
Pricing page does not state annual vs monthly billing.
